title: Interval coverage for population-adjusted synthesis with few studies
question: How does interval coverage of population-adjusted random-effects synthesis depend on the number of studies, when one individual-data trial supplies the adjusted contrast for several aggregate trials?
design: One individual-data trial transported by MAIC and 2 to 12 aggregate trials with heterogeneity; naive and two-step random-effects analyses with DerSimonian-Laird or Hartung-Knapp intervals. 18 cells, 2000 replicates each.
answer: Coverage fails in two ways. Meta-analyzing per-trial adjusted contrasts that reuse one individual-data trial as if independent lost coverage as trials were added (down to 0.55 at twelve trials with DerSimonian-Laird), because the shared error does not average out. Pooling the aggregate trials first and subtracting the transported contrast once fixed that; with DerSimonian-Laird it stayed within 0.93 to 0.97 from four trials, and Hartung-Knapp was conservative (up to 1.00) at two or three.
findings: Refuting sentence fails: coverage at two to four trials was 0.774 to 0.888 for the per-trial analysis and 0.909 to 0.962 for the two-step DerSimonian-Laird analysis.
Minimum trial count with coverage 0.93 to 0.97 at every heterogeneity level: 4 for two-step DerSimonian-Laird; none for the per-trial analyses or two-step Hartung-Knapp.
Per-trial analysis coverage fell with the number of trials even without heterogeneity.
not_answered: Pairwise synthesis with one individual-data trial; continuous outcome; no one-stage or Bayesian analysis; one overlap level. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: B versus A mean difference in the target population
